text.p: Investmentbank Austria Research revised down its 1997 net profit forecast for Polish builder Budimex to 17.6 million zlotys from 24.4 million and gave the firm a "reduce" rating, IB Austria said in a report.
Investmentbank Austria said its revision was necessary in part due to Budimex's 4.2 million zlotys in June provisions due to doubtful debts from a German partner.
"The magnitude of the provisions force us to further downgrade our forecast from 24.4 million zlotys to 17.6 million zlotys," said the weekly European Emerging Markets report.
The report, dated August 1, said Budimex's share price would remain vulnerable and subject to speculation until the company started to concentrate on profits rather than sales.
Late last month Budimex revised down its 1997 net profit forecast to 13 million from 23.5 million zloltys and group net to 18 million from 28 million zlotys.
Budimex said the revision was in part due to a downturn of the business cycle on the German and Czech markets and limited sales in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
The parent company made a net profit last year of 22.9 million zlotys.
